summary:
All four ratings are locked in on trends (91-69, 57%, n=160, 4W streak across R1-R4) and bullpen (88-72, 55%, n=160), and today's board is basically wall-to-wall consensus — 14 of 15 games have all four ratings agreeing on the same side, which is exactly the setup that's been printing money lately. R4 is the standout: its 14d strong-play window is 37-21 (64%, +24.0u) and its bullpen_fatigue cell is flagged HOT at +5.3pts over baseline, so lean into R4's confidence gaps. The clearest example is SFG @ LAD, where R4's +2.98 delta is the largest number on the whole slate and LAD as a liked team hits 69% (33-15, n=48) with a nasty 81% strong-play rate (25-6, +25.0u) — that's about as clean a green light as this model produces. TEX (+1.71 to +2.14 across all four ratings) and CLE (+1.36 to +1.58 consensus) are the next-strongest four-way agreements and neither team carries any red flags in the team logs.

Fade spots deserve attention too: NYY @ ARI is a unanimous NYY side, but NYY as a liked team is a losing proposition this year (21-20 straight, and strong plays are 8-12 for -3.0u) — if NYY grades out as a "strong" play tonight, that's a spot to trim stake size rather than chase the model blindly. Same caution on BAL, whose team-when-liked strong record is 8-11 (-3.0u); tonight's MIL @ BAL is the one SPLIT game on the board (R1-R3 lean BAL, R4 flips to MIL at -0.64), so treat it as a pass rather than a bet. Elsewhere, remember bullpen is on a 4L streak across all three legacy ratings (R1/R2/R3) despite the strong 14d rate — that's the one category where the recent number and the underlying momentum are in tension, so don't stack bullpen-driven plays without a second category behind them. Best combo agreement remains trends+sp at 57.3% (335-250) — TEX and PIT both get support from that pairing tonight given the SP matchups (Soriano vs Quantrill, Cameron vs Chandler) tilting in the same direction as the trend numbers.
